⁨⁩⁨kayg⁩⁨⁩ said:
> Finding/contract addition before implementation (D166): deleting inventory while automatic authenticated-channel attachment is enabled would otherwise recreate the removed member on reconnect. Add public removal tombstones keyed by authenticated host id. A channel reconnect/new node-local key cannot clear one. Only an explicit authorized mesh.node.enroll creating an unbound public-key inventory row permits rebinding and clearing the host tombstone. Member removal remains effective while offline; certificate expiry/transport loss do not remove membership. Migration 0019 gains this public table; removal records and inventory delete commit in the same writer transaction. No credential or private-key persistence. Existing Access enrollment permissions remain the grant source.

⁨⁩⁨kayg⁩⁨⁩ said:
> D215 round2 #129: proposed additive shared-writer queue contract before policy change.
> 
> A valid shared-writer sequenced Input whose unseen suffix exceeds currently available shared-queue space is deferred without changing accepted/written cursors, geometry or ownership segments. Each live peer retains at most one complete bounded frame plus one bounded socket-read suffix; later frames on that peer remain ordered behind it. Acceptance remains atomic when the full unseen suffix fits. The shim stops reading deferred peers, continues servicing other peers and PTY writes, and admits deferred requests fairly. Overlap is recalculated against the durable writer cursor before admission. Peer loss discards only unaccepted deferred data; already accepted input remains queued and the server replays unacknowledged data. Invalid ranges, malformed frames and requests violating ordering remain refusals. The shared accepted queue remains at most 1 MiB; deferred storage belongs only to at most 32 live peers, never to 512 retained identities. Peers without the negotiated SHARED_WRITER capability retain existing capacity-refusal behavior.
> 
> Reason: a bounded per-writer server flight alone cannot bound the aggregate surviving queue across retained identities. This applies backpressure without changing frozen frame layouts or choosing a new engine. Real PTY fail-first regression and bounded decoder/order tests will verify it.

⁨⁩⁨kayg⁩⁨⁩ said:
> D215 #129 additive shared-input reservation clarification before the follow-up repair.
> 
> A deferred shared Input must not globally disable reading ordinary peers: ReadFrom, InputStateRequest, Resize and duplicate input continue to parse and progress. Space reserved for the oldest deferred request is unavailable to fresh input from any peer. A peer without SHARED_WRITER that requests new input while that space is reserved receives its existing capacity refusal without cursor/geometry mutation; it does not gain deferred-input semantics. When one deferred frame succeeds and a later frame on the same socket defers, the later request receives a new queue ticket so it cannot overtake an already waiting peer.
> 
> Independent review found that the draft POLLIN guard currently blocks ordinary controls and can deadlock an output-blocked PTY before queued input drains. A corrected real-PTY fail-first regression is being executed against the immutable draft runner. Two-peer ordering coverage will verify renewed tickets. No frozen frame layout or foundational library change. Final module gates and real-terminal performance remain pending.


⁨⁩⁨kayg⁩⁨⁩ said:
> D215 #129 additive negotiation clarification before the ordinary native writer repair.
> 
> The SHARED_WRITER capability negotiates bounded queue deferral independently of selection mode. A supporting ordinary native writer should select this advertised capability while still using SelectWriter, so its input also waits for the surviving global queue instead of disconnecting. It does not use SelectSharedWriter or change ordinary replacement semantics. Old shims that do not advertise the capability retain their existing negotiated mask and capacity behavior.
> 
> Reason: the server16KiB durableAck window alone cannot bound the surviving1MiB queue across512 retained writer identities. Current connect_writer requests only bits0/1/2, so ordinary native paths could still receive a capacity refusal after detached writers left accepted bytes queued. Added a realUnix handshake fail-first regression for masks3/15 and unchanged ordinary selector; implementation will follow its observed red.
